title: TREM2: friend or foe in glioma?
title_zh: TREM2：胶质瘤中的朋友还是敌人？
abstract: Abstract Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) is a neuroimmune signaling hub involved in key cellular processes including microglial phagocytosis, chemotaxis, and inflammation. Dysregulation of TREM2 has been implicated in a variety of diseases, most notably in the innate immune response to neurodegenerative disorders and cancer. The TREM2 pathway plays a significant role in governing microglia phenotypic transitions in Alzheimer’s disease, as well as in regulating tumor-associated macrophages’ ability to modulate cytotoxic activity. However, TREM2’s role can be dependent on experimental parameters and disease contexts. Due to its intricate involvement in related disorders and the myeloid-dominated microenvironment in brain tumors, TREM2 has emerged as a vital player to better understand neuroimmune contributions to central nervous system malignancies. This review critically evaluates TREM2’s controversial function in gliomas, analyzes experimental and biological variables that may underlie divergent findings, and outlines important considerations for future investigations.
abstract_zh: 摘要：表达在髓系细胞上的触发受体2（TREM2）是一个神经免疫信号枢纽，参与微胶质细胞吞噬、趋化和炎症等关键细胞过程。TREM2失调已与多种疾病相关，尤其是在神经退行性疾病和癌症的先天免疫反应中。TREM2通路在阿尔茨海默病中调控微胶质细胞表型转变，并在调节肿瘤相关巨噬细胞的细胞毒活性方面发挥重要作用。然而，TREM2的功能可能取决于实验参数和疾病背景。鉴于其在相关疾病中的复杂作用以及大脑肿瘤中髓系细胞主导的微环境，TREM2已成为深入理解中枢神经系统恶性肿瘤神经免疫贡献的重要因素。本综述对TREM2在胶质瘤中的争议功能进行批判性评估，分析可能导致不同发现的实验和生物学变量，并概述未来研究的重要考量。
